svg.title: Data journey with Comet: the same four rows, Arrow arrays from file to file
svg.text: With Comet: columns from the source file to the target file
The same four lineitem rows, illustrative values; one of them fails the filter

g.text: Rust: work done once per Arrow batch
each column chunk: encoded pages (dictionary or plain), zstd-compressed; a row group holds one chunk per column
iceberg-rust decodes into Arrow arrays and applies the WHERE predicate: the grey 1994 row never leaves the scan
the mask is all true here, because the scan already filtered; the multiply runs on Decimal128 arrays
hashes for the whole key column at once; one slot per group in each state array; sums stay Decimal128
Arrow IPC block, lz4, for reducer A
Arrow IPC block, lz4, for reducer B
Murmur3 + pmod for the whole key column; each block is a small Arrow batch, one array per column
illustration: both orders land in one reduce task; in a real run they may not
Arrow arrays go straight into Parquet column pages
no rows, and no turn back to columns
encoded pages, zstd; IcebergCommit on the driver (iceberg-java) adds the file to a new snapshot
Shown with spark.comet.write.iceberg.enabled=true. With the default (false), the last steps run
as without Comet: CometColumnarToRow, then AppendData with iceberg-java's row writer.
